headline: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to 'Russia’s Google'
summary: The strikes hit two of Yandex's five data centers, including one housing supercomputers for its YandexGPT AI model. This has caused disruptions to various online services across Russia.
details: Ukrainian drone strikes have reportedly knocked out two of five data centers belonging to the Russian tech giant Yandex. One of the damaged facilities housed supercomputers crucial for training the company's YandexGPT AI model, impacting its chatbot and other online services.

The drone attacks occurred on October 8 and 9 in Russia's Sasovo and Kaluga regions. These actions were described by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as a "symmetrical response" to Russia's ongoing drone strike campaign targeting Ukraine's data centers.

The Ukrainian company Firepoint claimed its FP-1 one-way attack drones were involved in the strike on the Kaluga data center, Yandex's largest facility. The Sasovo attack specifically targeted a center housing two of Yandex's three supercomputers used for AI model training.

Yandex confirmed no employees were harmed but acknowledged disruptions to some services. Russian users reported issues accessing various platforms, including media websites, the Ivi video streaming platform, T-Bank digital banking, and Russian Railways.

Other impacted services included a dating app, a real estate aggregator, a self-publishing book platform, and the website of a top Russian professional soccer club. This incident highlights the increasing trend of data centers becoming wartime targets in 2026.

headline_marked: [[YouTuber visited by police]] after building camera to track cops
headline: YouTuber visited by police after building camera to track cops
summary: A YouTuber claims law enforcement visited his home after he developed a camera system designed to monitor police activity, similar to Flock Safety's controversial surveillance tech.
details: A YouTuber recently reported that law enforcement officials visited his residence following his creation of a camera system designed to track police vehicles. The system was explicitly modeled after Flock Safety's controversial automated license plate recognition (ALPR) technology.

Flock Safety cameras are widely used by police departments across the US to monitor traffic and aid in investigations, raising significant privacy concerns. The YouTuber's project aimed to turn the tables, applying similar surveillance methods to police activity.

The YouTuber's account suggests the visit was a direct response to his public disclosure of the project. This incident highlights the complex legal and ethical landscape surrounding public surveillance and counter-surveillance efforts.

This event sparks debate on the balance between public transparency, individual rights, and law enforcement operations. It questions who has the right to monitor whom in public spaces and the potential for technological tools to shift this dynamic.
